question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?

enhanced_information: The most likely nerve affected in this patient is the posterior interosseous nerve. The patient's symptoms of weakness in extending the middle finger, radial deviation on wrist extension, and tenderness distal to the lateral epicondyle are indicative of possible radial nerve involvement, specifically the posterior interosseous nerve.
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including weakness in extending the middle finger and radial deviation of the wrist upon extension, suggest an issue with the posterior interosseous nerve. This nerve is a branch of the radial nerve and is responsible for innervating the extensor muscles of the forearm. The lack of sensory impairment further supports this diagnosis, as the posterior interosseous nerve is primarily a motor nerve.
